title: Solar Panel Maintenance: How to Keep Your System Performing
excerpt: Simple maintenance tips to keep your solar panels running at peak efficiency, including cleaning, monitoring, and when to call a professional.
body:
## The Good News

Solar panels require very little maintenance. There are no moving parts, and most quality panels are designed to withstand hail, wind, and extreme heat. But a small amount of attention can keep your system performing at its best.

## Regular Checks

### Monitor Your Output
- Check your inverter or monitoring app weekly
- Look for sudden drops in generation
- Compare output to similar days in previous months
- Most modern systems send alerts if something goes wrong

### Visual Inspection
- Look for visible dirt, bird droppings, or leaf buildup
- Check for cracked or damaged panels after storms
- Ensure no new shading from growing trees
- Inspect roof mounting for any signs of rust or movement

## Cleaning Your Panels

### When to Clean
- Most panels self-clean with rainfall
- Clean if you notice visible grime or a performance drop
- Dusty or coastal areas may need cleaning 2-4 times per year
- Bird-heavy areas may need more frequent attention

### How to Clean Safely
- Use a garden hose from the ground — never pressure wash
- Clean early morning or late afternoon when panels are cool
- Never walk on panels or lean ladders against them
- Use soft brush with extension pole if hosing isn't enough
- Avoid abrasive cleaners or chemicals

### Professional Cleaning
- Costs $150-$400 depending on system size and access
- Recommended for multi-storey or hard-to-reach installations
- Some companies offer annual cleaning packages

## Inverter Maintenance

- Keep the area around your inverter clear and ventilated
- Check the display for error codes or warning lights
- String inverters typically last 10-15 years before replacement
- Microinverters last 20-25 years (same as panels)
- Budget $1,500-$3,000 for inverter replacement

## When to Call a Professional

- Significant drop in output that cleaning doesn't fix
- Error codes on your inverter
- Physical damage to panels after a storm
- Any electrical issues (flickering, tripping breakers)
- Annual health check recommended after warranty period

## Warranty Reminders

- Keep your installation paperwork and warranty certificates
- Most panel warranties are 25 years for performance
- Inverter warranties are typically 10-15 years
- Workmanship warranties from installers are usually 5-10 years
- Don't void your warranty by attempting electrical work yourself
